# 🚀 NGX Signal Utils

Source: https://github.com/dotted-labs/ngx-signal-utils/blob/main/README.md

<div align="center">

# 🚀 NGX Signal Utils

**Modern Angular state management with signals and @ngrx/signals**


_A comprehensive Angular utility suite providing extensive support for Angular signals and advanced features for the @ngrx/signals store, designed to enhance state management in modern Angular applications._

</div>

---

## ✨ Features

<table>
<tr>
<td width="50%">

### 📄 **Pagination Management**

- Smart pagination with entities support
- Local and remote pagination modes
- Built-in computed properties
- Seamless Bootstrap components integration

</td>
<td width="50%">

### 🧭 **Route & Query Params**

- Type-safe parameter handling
- Reactive route parameter tracking
- Automatic signal updates
- Router integration utilities

</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="50%">

### 📊 **Status Management**

- Loading, loaded, and error states
- Comprehensive state tracking
- Helper functions for state updates
- Async operation lifecycle management

</td>
<td width="50%">

### 🔧 **Developer Experience**

- Full TypeScript support
- Composable store features
- Tree-shakeable imports
- Zero configuration setup

</td>
</tr>
</table>

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Installation

```bash
npm install @dotted-labs/ngx-signal-utils
```

### Basic Usage

```typescript
import { signalStore } from '@ngrx/signals';
import { withEntities } from '@ngrx/signals/entities';
import { withPagination } from '@dotted-labs/ngx-signal-utils/pagination';
import { withStatus } from '@dotted-labs/ngx-signal-utils/status';

// Create a feature-rich store with pagination and status management
export const UserStore = signalStore(
  { providedIn: 'root' },
  withEntities<User>(),
  withPagination<User>({ isLocal: false }),
  withStatus(),
  withMethods((store) => ({
    async loadUsers() {
      patchState(store, setLoading());
      try {
        const users = await userService.getUsers({
          page: store.page(),
          pageSize: store.pageSize(),
        });
        patchState(store, setAllEntities(users.data), setTotalItems(users.total), setLoaded());
      } catch (error) {
        patchState(store, setError(error.message));
      }
    },
  })),
);
```

```typescript
// Use in your component
@Component({
  template: `
    <div *ngIf="userStore.isLoading()">Loading...</div>
    <div *ngIf="userStore.error()">{{ userStore.error() }}</div>

    <user-list [users]="userStore.currentPage()" />

    <pagination
      [page]="userStore.page()"
      [totalPages]="userStore.totalPages()"
      [hasNext]="userStore.hasNextPage()"
      [hasPrevious]="userStore.hasPreviousPage()"
      (pageChange)="changePage($event)"
    />
  `,
})
export class UsersComponent {
  userStore = inject(UserStore);

  ngOnInit() {
    this.userStore.loadUsers();
  }

  changePage(page: number) {
    this.userStore.changePage(page, () => this.userStore.loadUsers());
  }
}
```

## 📚 Feature Guides

<details>
<summary><strong>🔍 Pagination Feature</strong></summary>

### Complete Pagination Management

The pagination feature provides comprehensive pagination capabilities with both local and remote data handling.

```typescript
import { withPagination, setTotalItems } from '@dotted-labs/ngx-signal-utils/pagination';

export const ProductStore = signalStore(
  withEntities<Product>(),
  withPagination<Product>({ isLocal: true }), // Local pagination
);

// Available computed properties
productStore.isEmpty(); // boolean
productStore.hasNextPage(); // boolean
productStore.hasPreviousPage(); // boolean
productStore.totalPages(); // number
productStore.currentPage(); // Product[] (sliced for current page)

// Available methods
productStore.changePage(2, callback); // Navigate to page 2
productStore.changePageSize(20, callback); // Change items per page
```

**[📖 Full Pagination Documentation](./projects/ngx-signal-utils/pagination/README.md)**

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>🧭 Route & Query Parameters</strong></summary>

### Type-Safe Parameter Management

Handle route and query parameters with full type safety and reactive updates.

```typescript
import { withRouteParams, withQueryParams } from '@dotted-labs/ngx-signal-utils/route';

// Route: /users/:userId
export const UserDetailStore = signalStore(
  withRouteParams({
    userId: (param: string) => Number(param), // Transform to number
  }),
  withQueryParams({
    tab: (param?: string) => param || 'profile', // Default value
    sort: (param?: string) => (param as 'asc' | 'desc') || 'asc',
  }),
  withMethods((store) => ({
    // Access parameters in methods
    loadUser() {
      const userId = store.userId(); // number
      const tab = store.tab(); // string
      // ... load user logic
    },
    // Update query parameters
    switchTab(tab: string) {
      store.updateTab(tab); // Updates URL automatically
    },
  })),
);
```

**[📖 Full Route Parameters Documentation](./projects/ngx-signal-utils/route/README.md)**

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>📊 Status Management</strong></summary>

### Comprehensive State Tracking

Track loading states, errors, and success states with built-in utilities.

```typescript
import { withStatus, setLoading, setLoaded, setError } from '@dotted-labs/ngx-signal-utils/status';

export const ApiStore = signalStore(
  withStatus(),
  withMethods((store) => ({
    async fetchData() {
      patchState(store, setLoading());

      try {
        const data = await apiService.getData();
        patchState(store, { data }, setLoaded());
      } catch (error) {
        patchState(store, setError(error.message));
      }
    },
  })),
);

// Usage in templates
// apiStore.isLoading() -> boolean
// apiStore.isLoaded()  -> boolean
// apiStore.error()     -> string | null
```

**[📖 Full Status Management Documentation](./projects/ngx-signal-utils/status/README.md)**

</details>

## 🛠️ Requirements

- **Angular**: >=19.0.0
- **@ngrx/signals**: >=19.0.0
- **TypeScript**: >=5.8.0

## 🤝 Integration

### Works Great With

- **@ngrx/signals** - Core signal store functionality
- **Angular Router** - Automatic route parameter tracking

## 📖 API Reference

### Core Exports

```typescript
// Pagination
export { withPagination, setTotalItems, PaginationState } from '@dotted-labs/ngx-signal-utils/pagination';

// Route Management
export { withRouteParams, withQueryParams, ParamsConfig } from '@dotted-labs/ngx-signal-utils/route';

// Status Management
export { withStatus, setLoading, setLoaded, setError, StatusState } from '@dotted-labs/ngx-signal-utils/status';
```

# CLAUDE.md

Source: https://github.com/dotted-labs/ngx-signal-utils/blob/main/CLAUDE.md

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

This is an Angular library monorepo containing three main libraries:
- **ngx-signal-utils**: Angular signals utilities with advanced ngrx/signals store features
- **ngx-utils**: General Angular utilities (legacy, mostly deleted files)
- **ngx-bootstrap-components**: Bootstrap components for Angular (legacy, mostly deleted files)

The main focus is on `ngx-signal-utils`, which provides signal-based state management features for Angular applications.

## Core Architecture

### Library Structure
The `ngx-signal-utils` library is organized into modular features:
- **pagination/**: Pagination state management with entities support
- **route/**: Route and query parameter management
- **status/**: Loading/error status management

### State Management Pattern
All features use Angular's `@ngrx/signals` store with a consistent pattern:
- **withState()**: Defines initial state
- **withComputed()**: Derives computed values from state
- **withMethods()**: Provides state mutation methods
- **signalStoreFeature()**: Composes features together

Each feature exports both the feature factory function and utility functions for state updates.

### Core Dependencies
- Angular 19.x with signals support
- @ngrx/signals for state management
- TypeScript for type safety

## Development Commands

### Building
```bash
# Build all libraries
npm run build

# Build individual libraries
npm run build:ngx-signal-utils
npm run build:ngx-utils
npm run build:ngx-bootstrap-components
```

### Testing
```bash
# Run all tests
ng test

# Run tests for specific library
ng test ngx-signal-utils
```

### Linting
```bash
# Lint and fix the main library
npm run lint
```

### Publishing
```bash
# Publish all libraries (builds first)
npm run publish

# Publish individual libraries
npm run publish:ngx-signal-utils
npm run publish:ngx-utils
npm run publish:ngx-bootstrap-components
```

### Development
```bash
# Watch mode for development
npm run watch

# Start development server
npm start
```

## Key Implementation Patterns

### Feature Pattern
Each feature follows this structure:
```typescript
export function withFeatureName<T>(config?: Config) {
  return signalStoreFeature(
    withState<StateInterface>(initialState),
    withComputed((store) => ({
      // Computed properties from state
    })),
    withMethods((store) => ({
      // Methods to update state
    }))
  );
}
```

### State Update Functions
Provide utility functions for common state updates:
```typescript
export function setFeatureState(value: Type): StateInterface {
  return { /* state update */ };
}
```

### Type Configuration
Use generic types and configuration objects for flexible, type-safe APIs:
```typescript
export function withQueryParams<Config extends ParamsConfig>(config: Config)
```

## File Organization

- `src/public-api.ts`: Main entry point (currently empty)
- `[feature]/src/public_api.ts`: Feature-specific exports
- `[feature]/src/store/`: Store feature implementations
- `[feature]/src/states/`: State type definitions
- `[feature]/src/types/`: Shared type definitions

## Important Notes

- The main `src/public-api.ts` is currently empty and may need exports added
- Focus development on the `ngx-signal-utils` library as the other libraries appear to be legacy/deleted
- All features integrate with Angular's dependency injection system using `inject()`
- State features are designed to be composable and can be combined in stores
- Always maintain backward compatibility when making changes to public APIs

---

# CONTRIBUTING.md

Source: https://github.com/dotted-labs/ngx-signal-utils/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

## Contributing to NGX Bootstrap Components

We welcome contributions to the NGX Bootstrap Components library! Whether you're looking to fix bugs, add new features, or improve documentation, your help is appreciated. Here's how you can contribute:

### Getting Started

1. **Fork the repository** on GitHub.
2. **Clone your fork** to your local machine for development.

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/ngx-bootstrap-components.git
   cd ngx-bootstrap-components
   ```

3. **Install dependencies** to set up your development environment.

   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

### Making Changes

1. **Create a new branch** for your changes.

   ```bash
   git checkout -b your-feature-branch
   ```

2. **Make your changes** in the codebase. Ensure you adhere to the existing coding style and follow Angular's best practices.

3. **Test your changes** thoroughly. Add unit tests if applicable.

### Submitting Changes

1. **Commit your changes**. Write a clear, concise commit message that explains the purpose of your changes.

   ```bash
   git commit -am 'Add some feature'
   ```

2. **Push your changes** to your fork.

   ```bash
   git push origin your-feature-branch
   ```

3. **Submit a pull request** to the main repository. Provide a detailed description of your changes and reference any related issues.

### Code Review

1. Once your pull request is submitted, it will be reviewed by the maintainers. Be open to feedback and be prepared to make further improvements to your code.

2. **Address feedback** from the review. You may need to make changes and update your pull request.

### After Your Pull Request is Merged

Once your pull request is merged, you're officially a contributor! We encourage you to stay involved by:

- Helping to review other pull requests.
- Participating in discussions and providing feedback on the project.
- Continuing to contribute with more pull requests!

Thank you for contributing to NGX Bootstrap Components. Your efforts help make this library better for everyone!

## 🧑‍💻 Community

Join our community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/dotted-labs/ngx-bootstrap-components/issues) to connect with other contributors and discuss the future of the library.
